basics.name: Tristan Lazard
basics.label: Researcher at Microsoft Research
basics.summary: Researcher at Microsoft Research Health Futures in Cambridge, working on interpretability for scientific discovery in biology. After completing my undergraduate studies in biology at ENS Ulm, I pursued a Master's in Applied Mathematics at Sorbonne University, then earned my PhD from CBIO at Mines ParisTech / PSL University. My research bridges biology, mathematics, and computer science, with a focus on representation learning, model interpretability, and AI-driven biomarker discovery from large-scale microscopy images.

work.name: Microsoft Research, Health Futures
work.summary: Working on interpretability of large multimodal models for scientific discovery in biology. Contributing to agentic frameworks for automated histopathology analysis.

work.name: CBIO - Mines-Paristech
work.summary: During my PhD, I focused on training predictive models from Whole Slide Images of cancerous tissues. Besides their clinical use, my goal was to understand these models to improve our understanding of the disease. I also worked on developing unsupervised techniques to train representations of these biological samples. This effort resulted in 5 papers, 1 patent, and a prize-winning solution at an international data challenge, Visiomel.

work.name: CMM, Mines-Paristech
work.summary: In partnership with L’Or´eal, I created an algorithm for automatically counting melanocytes in microscopic images. This solution has been integrated into the processing pipeline and is now utilized in regular research.

work.name: IBPS, Sorbonne University, AIRE team
work.summary: I developed an algorithm for calculating phylogenetic trees from large-scale genetic sequence data (-omics data).

work.name: Collège de France, SMILE team
work.summary: I worked on a model of random mutualistic network. I studied its asymptotic behaviours and developed an algorithm to infer its parameters from a sampled network.

computing: ML+image processing libs (PyTorch, OpenCV, PIL, Sklearn)
